title: PKA: The Target Sets the Response

scenes.tts: Synthesis and breakdown set the cyclic AMP level. Once that messenger activates protein kinase A, why do heart and fat cells respond differently? The messenger is common, but the reachable machinery need not be. That is the puzzle.
scenes.caption: Synthesis and breakdown set the cAMP level. Once that messenger activates PKA, why do heart and fat cells respond differently? The messenger is common, but the reachable machinery need not be. That is the puzzle.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 cell cross-section and colour map without resetting. The GREY plasma membrane stays above the cytosol; cAMP remains GOLD, synthesis BLUE, breakdown RED. Add PKA as TEAL, regulatory subunits as PURPLE, compatible targets as GREEN, and other targets as muted GREY. Keep 'schematic' at lower right. The GOLD cAMP gauge from the first film holds steady, then transforms into several GOLD tokens approaching a large TEAL-PURPLE PKA complex. Pull back to show a heart-cell panel and fat-cell panel with different unanswered output icons. The question fills the top.
scenes.narration: Synthesis and breakdown set the cAMP level. Once that messenger activates PKA, why do heart and fat cells respond differently? The messenger is common, but the reachable machinery need not be. That is the puzzle.

scenes.visual: Over the carried cell world, show the title 'PKA: The Target Sets the Response' for two seconds. GOLD cAMP tokens drift, the TEAL-PURPLE complex breathes gently, and the two output icons remain question marks.

scenes.tts: At low cyclic AMP, protein kinase A rests as paired regulatory and catalytic subunits. Each catalytic subunit is a complete kinase. Each regulatory partner keeps one catalytic site inactive. The regulatory pair acts as an off switch until messenger arrives.
scenes.caption: At low cAMP, PKA rests as paired regulatory and catalytic subunits. Each catalytic subunit is a complete kinase. Each regulatory partner keeps one catalytic site inactive. The regulatory pair acts as an off switch until messenger arrives.
scenes.visual: Zoom until one PKA complex fills most of the frame. Build an R2C2 cartoon from labelled blocks: a PURPLE regulatory dimer in the centre and a TEAL catalytic block on each side. Put 'R2C2' and '4 subunits' on screen only. Each TEAL block has a large groove facing inward, occupied by a tab from PURPLE. Small OFF labels appear over the two grooves. No molecular structure is drawn.
scenes.narration: At low cAMP, PKA rests as paired regulatory and catalytic subunits. Each catalytic subunit is a complete kinase. Each regulatory partner keeps one catalytic site inactive. The regulatory pair acts as an off switch until messenger arrives.

scenes.tts: A kinase modifies a target protein by transferring phosphate from A T P. The target must enter a groove. A regulatory segment mimics a target and occupies that groove first. Blocking the groove prevents genuine targets from receiving phosphate.
scenes.caption: A kinase modifies a target protein by transferring phosphate from ATP. The target must enter a groove. A regulatory segment mimics a target and occupies that groove first. Blocking the groove prevents genuine targets from receiving phosphate.
scenes.visual: Magnify one TEAL catalytic block until its groove fills the frame. A GREEN target strip labelled 'substrate' approaches with an empty phosphate badge. Show an ATP chip near a separate pocket. Before the target docks, the PURPLE regulatory tab slides into the substrate groove. The GREEN strip bumps gently against it and waits. Labels read 'ATP pocket' and 'substrate groove'; no atom, bond or molecular ring appears.
scenes.narration: A kinase modifies a target protein by transferring phosphate from ATP. The target must enter a groove. A regulatory segment mimics a target and occupies that groove first. Blocking the groove prevents genuine targets from receiving phosphate.

scenes.tts: Cyclic AMP binds the regulatory subunits and changes their shape. Their blocking segments release the grooves. In the classical model, catalytic subunits come away free. Evidence suggests anchored complexes can act nearby without fully coming apart. Either picture exposes catalytic activity to targets within reach.
scenes.caption: cAMP binds the regulatory subunits and changes their shape. Their blocking segments release the grooves. In the classical model, catalytic subunits come away free. Evidence suggests anchored complexes can act nearby without fully coming apart. Either picture exposes catalytic activity to targets within reach.
scenes.visual: Return to the full PKA complex. GOLD cAMP tokens fill four on-screen sites labelled '4 cAMP sites'; the PURPLE blocks hinge outward and withdraw their tabs. Under 'classical model', the TEAL catalytic blocks move a short distance away. Then rewind that motion and transform the label to 'anchored complexes may remain associated'; the TEAL blocks stay tethered with exposed grooves. End with both model labels beside a question mark, so neither appears universal.
scenes.narration: cAMP binds the regulatory subunits and changes their shape. Their blocking segments release the grooves. In the classical model, catalytic subunits come away free. Evidence suggests anchored complexes can act nearby without fully coming apart. Either picture exposes catalytic activity to targets within reach.

scenes.tts: Now place the same active kinase across both cells. Both cells receive the same messenger level and display the same kinase. One cell offers green target strips, while the other offers different strips. Must their responses match?
scenes.caption: Now place the same active PKA across both cells. Both cells receive the same messenger level and display the same kinase. One cell offers green target strips, while the other offers different strips. Must their responses match?
scenes.visual: Pull back into two large cell panels sharing identical GOLD cAMP and TEAL active PKA. The left panel contains GREEN target strips with round ends; the right contains GREEN target strips with forked ends. Keep both output boxes blank. Across the top show 'Same cAMP + same PKA = same response?' with an empty choice marker. Targets bob toward the kinase but do not enter yet.
scenes.narration: Now place the same active PKA across both cells. Both cells receive the same messenger level and display the same kinase. One cell offers green target strips, while the other offers different strips. Must their responses match?

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep the equality question and both blank outputs visible. GOLD cAMP drifts, TEAL kinase grooves pulse, and the two target sets bob gently. Do not let any target dock or reveal an answer.

scenes.tts: No. An active kinase can modify only compatible targets it reaches. Different cells make different target proteins, so identical messenger and kinase activity can produce different cellular actions. The response follows the proteins present, not a special kind of cyclic AMP.
scenes.caption: No. An active PKA can modify only compatible targets it reaches. Different cells make different target proteins, so identical messenger and kinase activity can produce different cellular actions. The response follows the proteins present, not a special kind of cAMP.
scenes.visual: Replace the equality sign with a clear 'not necessarily'. In the left cell, round-ended GREEN strips dock, gain GOLD phosphate badges, and trigger a round output icon. In the right, forked GREEN strips dock and trigger a forked output icon. Muted GREY incompatible strips drift past without docking. Keep GOLD cAMP and TEAL PKA identical in both panels.
scenes.narration: No. An active PKA can modify only compatible targets it reaches. Different cells make different target proteins, so identical messenger and kinase activity can produce different cellular actions. The response follows the proteins present, not a special kind of cAMP.

scenes.tts: In fat, reachable targets include hormone-sensitive lipase and perilipin, supporting fat breakdown. In heart, other targets alter calcium entry, cycling, contraction, and relaxation. Liver offers another set, including enzymes that control glycogen. The relay is shared; the target set differs.
scenes.caption: In fat, reachable targets include hormone-sensitive lipase and perilipin, supporting fat breakdown. In heart, other targets alter calcium entry, cycling, contraction, and relaxation. Liver offers another set, including enzymes that control glycogen. The relay is shared; the target set differs.
scenes.visual: Transform the generic left cell into a labelled FAT cell while the other panel fades. Keep GOLD cAMP and TEAL PKA fixed. GREEN blocks labelled 'hormone-sensitive lipase' and 'perilipin' receive phosphate badges beside a fat-droplet icon that releases fuel droplets. Then morph the same cell into HEART: the target blocks become 'L-type Ca²⁺ channel / Rad', 'phospholamban' and 'troponin I', each feeding an output arrow labelled 'calcium entry', 'calcium cycling' or 'contraction + relaxation', and a schematic contraction bar strengthens then relaxes. On the liver sentence, briefly replace those blocks with one label, 'glycogen-control enzymes'.
scenes.narration: In fat, reachable targets include hormone-sensitive lipase and perilipin, supporting fat breakdown. In heart, other targets alter calcium entry, cycling, contraction, and relaxation. Liver offers another set, including enzymes that control glycogen. The relay is shared; the target set differs.

scenes.tts: Reach also matters within one cell. An anchoring protein can hold protein kinase A beside a selected substrate. The address narrows which target can meet the active kinase. Nearby cyclase supplies messenger, while nearby phosphodiesterase removes it.
scenes.caption: Reach also matters within one cell. An anchoring protein can hold PKA beside a selected substrate. The address narrows which target can meet the active kinase. Nearby adenylyl cyclase supplies cAMP, while nearby phosphodiesterase removes it.
scenes.visual: Merge the panels into one large cell. Build one neighbourhood at left: a WHITE scaffold labelled 'anchoring protein' holds TEAL PKA beside one GREEN substrate. A BLUE membrane cyclase above releases GOLD cAMP locally. A RED phosphodiesterase below makes nearby GOLD tokens fade. Slide the whole five-part assembly to the right and leave a faint address marker behind, showing that another local assembly can occupy a different site without drawing a hard wall.
scenes.narration: Reach also matters within one cell. An anchoring protein can hold PKA beside a selected substrate. The address narrows which target can meet the active kinase. Nearby adenylyl cyclase supplies cAMP, while nearby phosphodiesterase removes it.

scenes.tts: Experiments reveal local cyclic AMP regions and receptor-specific protein kinase A activity. Local production, local removal, binding, and restricted movement may all contribute. Their importance varies and remains debated. The local patterns are observed; the mechanism is not fully settled.
scenes.caption: Experiments reveal local cAMP regions and receptor-specific PKA activity. Local production, local removal, binding, and restricted movement may all contribute. Their importance varies and remains debated. The local patterns are observed; the mechanism is not fully settled.
scenes.visual: Keep the one-cell world. Animate four candidate influences around the local GOLD cloud without selecting a winner: a BLUE local source, a RED local sink, PURPLE binding blocks that briefly hold GOLD tokens, and GREY intracellular obstacles that make paths wind. Label each with a question-mark badge and group them under 'candidate contributors'. A separate bright label reads 'local responses observed'. Never show a wall, absolute confinement, or one mechanism as sufficient.
scenes.narration: Experiments reveal local cAMP regions and receptor-specific PKA activity. Local production, local removal, binding, and restricted movement may all contribute. Their importance varies and remains debated. The local patterns are observed; the mechanism is not fully settled.

scenes.tts: Activation therefore opens the catalytic groove, but access gives the signal meaning. The text now tests that groove with competition and examines the evidence for local signalling. Those experiments separate what is established from what is proposed.

scenes.visual: Zoom from the whole cell back to one exposed TEAL catalytic groove beside a GREEN compatible target. Behind it, the two local neighbourhoods remain faintly visible. Transform the groove into a simple competition setup with one target waiting and a blank result panel, without answering the text's inhibitor prediction. Then pull the camera back enough to show the observed local GOLD clouds with the four candidate-contributor question marks still unresolved.

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'PKA responses depend on which targets are nearby.' Set it large and centred on the dark background. No title, logo, URL, subtitle or smaller line appears. A TEAL kinase stays centred while different GREEN targets drift within reach and muted GREY targets remain distant.
